scope: Native LDS/LES/LFS/LGS/LSS source interfaces: Clang exposes 13 packed far-pointer builtins; NeverC exposes LDS/LES word/dword forms and qualifies all ten Linux i386 forms through full LLVM. Existing nine long-mode forms remain qualified.
build_note: Binaries were built from these source contents before the commits were created. Tool hashes identify the qualified binaries. No machine lowering or instruction-effect definition was changed.

limitations: The protected qualification is CPL0 code16/code32 with a 32-bit stack and pointer ABI; real mode, VM86, CPL3 alignment checking and asynchronous events are excluded.
NeverC Linux i386 emits IR for the full LLVM fork. Its embedded i386 machine backend, code16 frontend and other i386 platform frontends remain unavailable.
Only ABI-compatible protected successes return through the compiler frame; arbitrary segment/stack/TLS replacement is not an ordinary C continuation.
x64 null selectors 1..3 are observed at the immediate ptrace stop; Linux signal return can clear them and is not qualified as instruction continuation.
Descriptor accessed-bit effects are observed, but privileged descriptor-write-fault and arbitrary machine-state continuation qualification is not established by this batch.
ELF/COFF/Mach-O frontend and assembly profiles passed; physical execution is Linux x64 and Linux KVM protected mode, not Windows or macOS runtime.
No NeverD execution or renderer semantics changed; its general i386 state/source dispatcher and remaining SMM/SGX/fault/event gaps are still open.
